article.title: Whom Did God Give Land
article.author: Paul deLespinasse
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Disputes over land have long riled the human race. A popular argument has been that a particular group was given rights to land by God. Numerous passages in Genesis, the first book of the Bible’s Old Testament, assert that God gave particular lands forever to the people now referred to as Israelis. In Exodus 3:7-8 we are told: “And the LORD said, I have surely seen the affliction of my people which are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters; for I know their sorrows; “And I am come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land unto a good land and a large, unto a land flowing with milk and honey; unto the place of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites.” Interestingly, there were already people (the Canaanites, and others) living in this promised land. If God was giving this land to the Israelis, did this mean that it was exclusively theirs, or that they would be its privileged class? What about the Canaanites and other groups already living there? Could they be expelled? Were they not equally children of God? This is not merely an historical question. This issue still comes up today. In Israel substantial numbers of people think that God’s alleged donation gives them exclusive rights to occupy the area, and that other people can legitimately be killed or forced to leave. Similar attitudes exist among many Palestinians, who descend from people already living in the area when holocaust survivors moved there after World War II. Their controversial slogan “From the river to the sea, Palestine will be free” refers to all of the territory between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea including all of present day Israel. Related: Bombers or Solar Panels? The Real Cost of America's Military Priorities The issue is also with us in other parts of today’s world. Various indigenous peoples movements claim that their rights based on priority were violated by all the illegal European aliens moving into the Americas and Australia. In various circles today Land Acknowledgments apologize for this “injustice.” In the United States today there are also people who believe that descendants of their European ancestors who arrived in the past have the right to make it illegal for new people to move in. In effect, they too are claiming a God-given right to exclusive residency. It seems to me that the Bible, written by human beings and reflecting human views, can sometimes get things wrong, and that the claim that God gave territory exclusively to the descendants of Abraham was just plain wrong. Why would a just God do any such thing? The writers may have allowed their political interests to override any actual messages they were receiving from on high. As Thomas Hobbes noted in his Leviathon (1651), “If Livy say the Gods once made a cow speak, and we believe him not, we distrust not God therein, but Livy.” The Russian Orthodox church may have a good idea here. My Russian Bible calls the New Testament the Новый Завет (Novy Zavet), using the standard Russian term for “new.” But it calls what we call the Old Testament the Вехтий Завет (Bekty Zavet), not using Старый (starry) , the usual Russian term for “old.” I had to look the new term up, and it translates as “ decrepit ” or “ worn out .” “Worn out” may be too strong for the Old Testament in general, but it could be about right for its discussion of land grants. This religious belief has had terrible consequences throughout human history. Related: The Impossible Will Take a Little While: The Power of Persistence Let’s assume there is a just God who created the universe and everything in it. It makes more sense to conclude that land is given, not to particular groups of people, but to the human race in general. If this is true, it means that indigenous peoples who occupy territory have no natural right to exclude other people from moving in. (However, it does not excuse the atrocious behavior of the new settlers towards the people already living there.) It also means that today’s Americans have no natural right to exclude other people from moving in, to treat them very shabbily, and to force many of them to go somewhere else. It has been human beings, not God, who divided the world up into separate territories. It is up to us to correct this mistake.
